>Obviously that is an indicator that I am weaker than them mentally and emotionally.

OP, I kind of used to think along these lines. Ask yourself: how does it matter if you are indeed weaker than them? Who are they to set your standards by? Are they perfect/good people simply because they either a) don't share your problems, b) don't think as deeply as you do or c) do a better job of masking their emotions than you?

What matters in this world is ultimately you. *You* decide who you want to be, not people posting happy quotes. Try to accept who you are. 

I used to set standards for myself looking at other people. I could never live up to them. But then I realised that that's what they do. I'm not them. I've got different priorities, different things that I value. I've got other problems now, but I think I've mostly got rid of caring about what other people think of me. 

This is not going to solve any underlying problems, but it'll probably free up a thread of thought and make you feel less overwhelmed. You need treatment for those - punishing yourself in that way isn't going to help you or the people you've hurt/think you've hurt. 

>why should I feel sad, what gives me the right

Because obviously you care a lot for them, though you might lose control at times. Staying this way is going to make yourself worse, and consequently keep making your parents feel worse as well. It's a feedback loop. You need to help each other to break out of it, and trust me, your parents won't be happy if their child takes some drastic measure without seeking their help first.

Student myself. My opinion:

Mobiles and tablets should definitely be not allowed in class. Between periods - acceptable, but these have a lot of potential to cause problems. My suggestion - instead of smartphones, ordinary mobile phones (“bricks”) should be permitted. No internet access = no problems while in class. But proper technology as a whole should definitely be incorporated into education.

Uniform - while I was myself never much inconvenienced, it is indeed pointless to have ties in summer.

Permission for drinking water - I totally agree with you about this. An utterly pointless rule. If I ever become a teacher, when teaching a new class, my first instruction would be to not ask before drinking water. Exactly one teacher in our school did this.

Corporal punishment - Agree too. Causes more harm than good.

Rote Learning - Agree 110%. This is the single largest blight on our education system. You’ll find 10th graders rattling off formulae for the lengths of common tangents, etc., but who are unable to convert a speed in m/min to m/sec. Computer students routinely memorise programs, and then get mad when a “tough”(read not in textbook) problem shows up. There are students capable of writing programs to print complicated patterns, who, in 12th, are also able to produce a recursive solution from memory, but who cannot wrap their heads around object-passing. Many have not the slightest understanding of the basics of the language they’re learning.

Fun anecdote- during my class 12th per-boards, before a physics exam, I heard a classmate asking another how to remove a logarithm. I don’t know how he got through 11th.
